parsed.modern: HELM of a ship, is a piece of timber fastened into the rudder, which comes forward into the steering, or place where the person at the helm steers the ship, by holding the whipstaff in his hand, which is joined to the helm. They begin however to be left off, steering-wheels being used in their room.
